ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every director, officer, shareholder, and individual with significant control against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, the PCMLTFA-defined foreign and domestic politically exposed persons (PEPs), including heads of international organizations, and prudent US OFAC SDN/sectoral screening as counterparty risk. Enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs, including ministerial, judicial, military, legislative, state-owned enterprise, and political party leadership roles; enhanced measures include senior management approval, verification of source of wealth and source of funds, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Screening must be repeated on a risk-triggered basis at least every two years and immediately upon any material change in ownership, address, or status.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry, operated by Service Alberta and accessible through licensed Alberta registry agents, with the official website at www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry and NUANS-based corporate name search through the Government of Canada's NUANS system.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be filed in Latin script. English or French forms are accepted, and where a name contains non-English, non-French, or non-Latin elements, an accurate English/French transliteration must be supplied for registry indexing. The name must include an acceptable legal element, such as 'Limited', 'Incorporated', 'Corporation', 'Ltd.', 'Inc.', 'Corp.', or the French-language equivalents, and must not be confusingly similar to any existing corporate, business, or trade name recorded in the Alberta or Canadian NUANS database.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, banker, banking, trust, loan, insurance, assurance
Credit union, loan corporation, trust corporation, financial services institution
University, college, institute, academy, or polytechnic where reference is made to education
Engineer, engineering, geoscientist, or professional engineering designations
Lawyer, barrister, solicitor, legal practitioner, or legal services
Real estate, realtor, brokerage, property management, or real estate trading terms that may imply regulated conduct under the Real Estate Act
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file a written reconsideration or administrative review request with the Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of the rejection, attaching a fresh NUANS report and a statement explaining distinctive elements, degree of similarity, and any regulatory consents already obtained. A name reservation generally expires after 90 days; an extension or renewal may be sought by filing a new reservation request or, where the registry allows, an application to extend the reservation before expiry. If administrative reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review under the applicable Alberta Rules of Court. In practice, a rejected name can be modified and resubmitted with a new NUANS search without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable for this PropTech SaaS entity provided it supplies a physical street address in Alberta at which service of process can be accepted, mail is forwarded, and the address is identified as the registered office in the Articles of Incorporation. A P.O. Box or mail-only address is not permissible. Because the entity holds no statutory real estate brokerage licence and offers software as a service, no physical commercial location is required; however, the registered office arrangement must be supported by jurisdiction-specific records in the corporate minute book.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk: approximately 10% for the first year for a non-licensed SaaS/proptech company with a virtual registered office and no physical commercial premises. The likelihood rises above 20% if the Canada Revenue Agency, Alberta Corporate Registry, or FINTRAC receives complaints, flags anomalous financial flows, or questions commercial substance for residency or tax treaty purposes.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended; incorporation under s.17 and s.18; registered office under s.101; directors and officers under ss.109-112 and ss.137-139; corporate records under s.103.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Corporate Registration Division, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation together with Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed for an Alberta business corporation. The corporation may issue common shares for nominal consideration or with designated stated capital. No escrow account or paid-up capital deposit is required at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the corporation accept the outstanding share subscription and allot the subscribed common shares as set out in the subscription schedule. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the corporation be and is hereby established at the Alberta address in the Articles of Incorporation, and that the Notice of Registered Office be filed. RESOLVED, that [Name], [Name], and [Name] be appointed as the first directors and officers, with [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary-Treasurer, and [Name] as Director, each to serve until successors are chosen. RESOLVED, that the directors and officers are authorized to execute all necessary filings, banking resolutions, and ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Name Search System (online through Service Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a pre-incorporation name search using an Alberta Name Search report or obtain a NUANS report through an authorized Alberta Corporate Registry agent. Select a name that is distinguishable from existing corporate and trade names and does not contain prohibited or misleading language. If a specific name is preferred, reserve the name before filing the Articles of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Name search request form or NUANS report dated within 90 days
Consent letter for any distinctive or protected words used in the proposed name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit alternative names, provide a written explanation of distinguishability, or request administrative review of the name search decision before filing articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting Articles of Incorporation and Statutory Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator, legal counsel, or authorized corporate service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), setting out the corporation name, share structure, and restrictions if any. Prepare the Notice of Registered Office and the Notice of Directors. Require each proposed director to execute a consent and acknowledge the duties described in the Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any drafting deficiencies identified by the registry or a corporate service provider, obtain updated consents, and re-execute the articles before statutory filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) or an authorized Registry Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Articles of Incorporation, Notice of Registered Office, and Notice of Directors with the Alberta Corporate Registry. Pay the applicable government filing fee. Upon approval, receive the Certificate of Incorporation and the online corporate registry summary.
required_dossiers: Name search report or reservation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice, correct the articles or notices and resubmit within the stated cure period; a returned filing may be refiled with the same filing date if all deficiencies are cured promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency — Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with the Canada Revenue Agency to obtain a Business Number (BN) and any required program accounts, including the corporate income tax account, GST/HST account, payroll account, and import/export account if applicable. Provide the certificate of incorporation and corporate details in the registration application.
required_dossiers: Registered office and records office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries or rejects the registration, correct the business information through the Business Registration Online portal, call the CRA Business Assistance line, or file the appropriate RC1 form to complete program account registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, By-laws and Share Allotment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting of the board of directors. Adopt the corporation's initial by-laws, appoint officers, approve the share subscription and allotment, issue share certificates, adopt a corporate seal if desired, and approve the opening of the corporate bank account. Record proceedings in written minutes or a unanimous directors' resolution.
required_dossiers: Corporate bank account requisition and KYC documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any director or officer appointment is defective, execute a unanimous shareholders' resolution or hold a second board meeting to ratify and cure the appointment before relying on corporate authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Records and Municipal Operational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Secretary and applicable municipal licensing authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish the corporate records book and registers at the registered office in Alberta, including the share register and director register. Confirm the records office address with the Alberta Corporate Registry. If the corporation leases physical premises, obtain the required municipal business licence and applicable occupancy or fire-safety clearances.
required_dossiers: Notice of Change of Registered Office if the initial address changes
Municipal business licence application (only if a physical office is maintained)
Lease or occupancy permit if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a registered office or records address is found deficient, file a Notice of Change of Registered or Records Office with the Alberta Corporate Registry and update the minute book. A municipal licence denial may be cured by providing proof of lawful occupancy and fire-safety compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable for pure SaaS and PropTech software operations; a municipal business licence may apply only if a physical office is maintained.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), federal authority for GST/HST under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act and for Part I corporate income tax. Operational portals: Business Registration Online (BRO) and CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html). Alberta corporate income tax (Alberta Corporate Tax Act) is administered and collected by the CRA on behalf of Alberta; Alberta corporate registration is administered through Service Alberta / Alberta Registries (CORES).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate under the Alberta Business Corporations Act (or federal CBCA with Alberta extra-provincial registration) via the Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES); certificate issued within 1-3 business days. Step 2: CRA automatically issues the 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) upon incorporation confirmation. Step 3: Add the GST/HST program account (RT suffix) through Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1; registration is mandatory if taxable supplies made in Canada (including zero-rated supplies) exceed C$30,000 over any four consecutive calendar quarters (ETA s. 240); voluntary registration is available for input tax credit recovery. Step 4: Register the corporate income tax program account (RC suffix) - automatic for resident corporations; open CRA My Business Account and authorize a representative via a RepID. Step 5: For non-resident directors or shareholders, maintain an Alberta agent for service of process when applicable. No minimum capital, stamp duty, or notarization is required; typical turnaround is 3-10 business days for BN issuance plus GST account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Canadian business corporation is a separate taxpayer for federal and Alberta corporate income tax, with no flow-through treatment. For indirect tax purposes, the corporation is an independent GST/HST registrant. Territorial_Scope nuance: Alberta is a non-participating province (non-HST, no provincial sales tax); the combined indirect tax headline rate in Alberta is the 5% federal GST only. No tax-exempt free-zone status applies to any Alberta location.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box classification exists domestically; a Canadian corporation is treated as a per se corporation for US federal tax purposes (Treas. Reg. sec. 301.7701-2(b)(8)(i)). Relevant elections and mechanisms: (i) ITA s. 85(1) rollover election on property transfers to the corporation; (ii) ITA s. 89(14) eligible dividend designation; (iii) ITA s. 45(2) election to defer capital gains on real estate change of use; (iv) ETA s. 156 election for nil consideration on closely related intra-group supplies; (v) ETA s. 273(1) joint election for closely related GST registrants; (vi) ITA s. 261 functional-currency election aligning USD/ACH revenue streams. Hybrid mismatch anti-avoidance: ITA s. 18.4 (excess interest) and ss. 94.1-94.4 apply; no elective hybrid-neutrality regime is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms_note: Not applicable - no further elective classification beyond the above is available for a Canadian-resident corporation under federal or Alberta law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST - Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (Excise Tax Act, Part IX). In Alberta the applicable system is federal GST at 5%, with no provincial HST or PST component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 (taxable supplies, including zero-rated supplies, made in Canada over any four consecutive calendar quarters; supplies made outside Canada - such as zero-rated services relating to foreign real estate supplied to non-resident customers - are excluded from the threshold test). Voluntary GST/HST registration is permitted at any time; the simplified non-resident digital-services registration uses the same C$30,000 de minimis threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No continuous transaction control (CTC) or real-time fiscal clearance / digital stamping regime is in force in Canada. The CRA does not pre-clear or pre-validate invoices. GST/HST returns must generally be filed electronically (NETFILE/TELEFILE/XML via My Business Account API); large registrants use EDI/XML interfaces. Invoices must contain prescribed content under the ETA Information Returns Regulations: seller identity, BN and RT program account, invoice date, description, consideration, GST rate and amount. A voluntary PEPPOL-based national e-invoicing framework is under phased rollout but is not a statutory clearance requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Services supplied to a non-resident person are zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7 ETA unless: (i) the non-resident is a GST registrant; (ii) the service relates to real property situated in Canada; or (iii) the service relates to tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed. For this PropTech SaaS (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 531390 - property management and rental screening cloud), 0% GST applies to subscription services supplied to non-resident customers for non-Canadian real estate. If the platform supports Canadian real property, even for non-resident owners, the supply is taxable at 5% GST and zero-rating is unavailable. Digital/cloud supplies are further governed by Part 2 of Schedule IX place-of-supply rules: supplies of intangibles to Canadian-resident individuals are deemed made in Canada, and B2B supplies are generally taxed where the Canadian recipient's normal place of consumption is situated in Canada. Substantiation follows ETA s. 180 and CRA GST/HST Memorandum 17-1 (Proof of Export / secondary evidence policy).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA B13A export declaration and bill of lading or air waybill (required only for tangible goods export; not applicable to pure SaaS delivery)
SaaS master subscription agreement / SOW identifying the non-resident customer, Canadian GST status, and the real property locations covered
Commercial invoice marked 'Zero-rated - Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7 ETA' and bearing the corporation's GST/HST RT program account number

Inward remittance certificate / SWIFT MT103 credit advice, ACH settlement report, or Stripe Billing payout record evidencing inbound FX payment within a prudential 180-day benchmark (Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds repatriation deadline)
Service delivery evidence: usage logs, API access records, tenant-screening report delivery confirmations, and IP-geolocation data for the non-resident customer
Non-resident self-certification / beneficial ownership questionnaire for B2B customers
Contemporaneous export dossier retained for six years under ETA s. 286 books-and-records requirements
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds repatriation deadline; the 180-day figure is a documentary-evidence benchmark adopted for diligence. The CRA may reassess a zero-rating claim within four years of the filing date (ETA s. 298(2)), extended to eight years where misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud is established. If export evidence is deficient, the CRA reverses the 0% treatment, reassesses at 5% GST, charges compound daily interest at CRA prescribed rates, and applies the ETA s. 285.1 civil false-statement penalty equal to the greater of C$250 and 50% of the net tax understated. Knowingly false export claims are prosecuted under ETA s. 327 with fines of 50%-200% of evaded tax and imprisonment up to five years on indictment; directors and officers are jointly and severally liable under ETA s. 323 for unremitted amounts. CRA Memorandum 17-1 secondary-evidence policy is applied strictly: secondary evidence is accepted only where original documentation was lost and all reasonable efforts to obtain replacements are demonstrated. Claimed input tax credits and refunds are subject to offset and clawback under ETA s. 292; repeated failures trigger the exporter review-flag protocol and mandatory full-scope GST audits.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties_no: Non-arm's-length foreign SaaS customers also invite income-tax transfer-pricing review under ITA s. 247; contemporaneous documentation of intercompany export pricing is recommended alongside the indirect-tax export dossier.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential regulation of banks and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/ATF supervision. Canada maintains no dedicated foreign-exchange administration or exchange-control department; external monetary policy is discharged via the Bank of Canada Act and the Currency Act, and banking market entry/foreign bank operations are licensed under the Bank Act (Schedule I, II, and III status).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible pursuant to Article VIII, Sections 2-4 of the IMF Articles of Agreement. Both current-account and capital-account transactions (foreign direct investment, share subscription, intercompany financing, principal and interest servicing, and profit/dividend repatriation) are unrestricted and require no central-bank approval, license, or repatriation computation. The only fiscal friction on outbound profit remittance is non-resident withholding tax under Part XIII of the Canadian Income Tax Act: 25% statutory, usually reduced to 5-15% under Canada's tax treaties (e.g., under Article X of the Canada-US Treaty, 5% on dividends where the US beneficial owner is a corporation holding at least 10% of voting shares; 15% generally; 0% on certain interest under the parent-subsidiary exemption). For CA_CORP, an Alberta Business Corporation with a PropTech SaaS revenue model, no surplus-capital test, no dividend-blocking statute, and no 'capital account registration' obligation (as encountered in EMEA/LATAM regimes) applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada abolished statutory foreign-exchange controls in 1951 and has never re-imposed surrender or repatriation obligations. Exporters of services and digital goods, including cross-border PropertyTech subscription revenue flowing through Stripe Billing and ACH Direct rails, may retain 100% of foreign-currency proceeds indefinitely in either CAD or foreign-currency operating accounts. There is no mandated timeline for conversion, no minimum conversion ratio, and no obligation to channel export receipts through an authorized dealer. The only administrative overlay is the Bank of Canada / Statistics Canada International Transactions Reporting requirement: resident corporations must report cross-border receipts and payments above prescribed thresholds to Statistics Canada for balance-of-payments statistical purposes, and Canadian banks apply standardized purpose-of-payment codes on cross-border wires; these are statistical and prudential recording measures, not exchange-control measures.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability as a secondary clearing overlay, but not as the principal treasury bank for capital escrow or long-term liquidity. Wise (Wise Payments Canada), Payoneer, Airwallex, Stripe Treasury (via Stripe Payments Canada), and Mercury (US-based) are operational in Canada; however, under the Bank Act a non-bank entity cannot accept Canadian 'deposits' in the legal sense, cannot be a member of the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC), and must settle each electronic payment through a settlement account held at a Canadian Payments Act member bank. The Retail Payment Activities Act (S.C. 2021, c. 23), with regulations phased in commencing 2024, requires all non-bank payment service providers to register with the Bank of Canada, safeguard funds in trust/escrow, maintain operational incident plans, and comply with FINTRAC registration as Money Service Businesses (MSBs) under the PCMLTFA. Recommended architecture for ISIC_6201 (PropTech SaaS): Stripe Billing and ACH Direct rails collect USD/CAD subscription payments, funds settle through the fintech's Canadian settlement bank, and daily treasury sweeps move balances into the CA_CORP Schedule I bank operating and escrow accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For Canadian-resident directors and signing officers, remote account opening is generally available through online video KYC at most Schedule I banks (RBC, TD, BMO, CIBC, Scotiabank, ATB), particularly because the Alberta corporate registry record is publicly verifiable. For non-resident directors or remote UBOs, in-person attendance at a corporate banking branch is normally mandated for original document inspection and signature verification under FINTRAC's account-opening and record-keeping obligations in the PCMLTFA. Remote opening for non-resident directors is available only via dedicated international desks (e.g., RBC International Banking Centre, CIBC Cross-Border, BMO Global Business) and typically requires: (i) apostilled or notarized corporate documents certified within 90 days; (ii) original passport-grade identification verified by an independent notary; (iii) a completed Alberta Beneficial Ownership Information Report; and (iv) Canadian legal opinion confirming director and officer authority. Given CA_CORP's non-resident ownership allowance and zero minimum capital requirement, the lowest-friction onboarding strategy is to appoint at least one Alberta-resident director/signing officer for the operational accounts while keeping non-resident UBOs fully disclosed on the registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) or non-resident director as authorized signatory; foreign nexus triggers enhanced due diligence under PCMLTFA and OSFI Guideline B-10.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled Certificate of Incorporation from the Alberta Registrar of Companies; unexpired Alberta Beneficial Ownership Information Report; certified Board Resolutions from the corporate minute book; full upstream organizational chart to the natural-person UBO; notarized passport/government ID for each UBO; source-of-funds declaration with audited foreign parent financial statements (if >25% holding); tax-residency self-certifications (W-8BEN-E for US investors / Canadian NR301 for treaty claims); and a Canadian counsel legal opinion on corporate authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cryptocurrency, digital-token, or unverifiable electronic-asset proceeds intended for share capital, escrow, or subscription funding in a real-estate technology platform.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete fiat on/off-ramp transaction records from FINTRAC-registered MSB exchanges; Chainalysis/TRM Labs blockchain tracing reports covering the prior 24 months; a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA Canada) comfort letter confirming the economic substance and source of paid-up capital; a board resolution recording the capital injection and its business purpose; source-of-wealth statements for each contributor; and a no-encumbrance legal opinion confirming the funds are not derived from third-party lending or unregistered securities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and trade-control exposure: counterparties with high-risk jurisdictional nexus, including Canada-China-US cross-border software licensing and data-center arrangements; triggered under OSFI Guideline B-11, UN and Canadian sanctions lists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Denied Party Screening outputs for all contractors, tenants, data providers, and UBOs, benchmarked to the consolidated Canadian sanctions list, UN Security Council resolutions, and OFAC SDN list; a client/tenant risk assessment questionnaire with a clear commercial narrative; distribution agreements containing pass-through sanctions and OFAC-representation clauses; end-user certifications; and a 12-month KYC refresh evidence pack.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or PEP family member appearing as investor, shareholder, or high-value tenant-data partner of the PropTech platform.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINTRAC-compliant foreign/domestic PEP self-declaration forms; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation; independent verification letters from a regulated Canadian financial adviser or lawyer; a full beneficial-ownership chain identifying the PEP nexus; enhanced monitoring consent; and a signed periodic re-certification undertaking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-arm's-length cross-border intercompany payments (royalties, technology service fees, management fees) flagged by the bank's AML/FX desk for potential tax 'stripping' or CRA transfer-pricing review under Section 247 and subsection 18(4).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contemporaneous Canadian transfer-pricing documentation (Form T106 Supplementary Disclosure and supporting TP study); OECD-aligned intercompany agreements with cost-contribution and fee-benchmark narratives; a transfer-pricing benchmark opinion prepared by a Canadian CPA firm; and a parent-company tax indemnity/comfort letter confirming arm's-length terms.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route inbound equity/loan proceeds as a SWIFT MT103 single-customer credit transfer from the foreign investor or venture fund into the CA_CORP CAD-denominated Capital Escrow Account at the selected Schedule I bank. Wire instructions must include: (i) beneficiary legal name and account number exactly matching the Alberta corporate registry record; (ii) the beneficiary bank's SWIFT/BIC and 9-digit Canadian Clearing Code (CC); and (iii) the appropriate Canadian Payments Association purpose-of-payment code - for equity subscription use 'XR' (Equity Investment / Securities Purchase); for intercompany shareholder loans use 'XL' (Intercompany Financing); for B2B software subscription collections use 'XT' (Services, Business). On the US side, US-dollar investments are routed via Fedwire/CHIPS into the bank's USD cross-border account and converted to CAD at the bank's prevailing rate unless a commercial FX forward is pre-arranged. Verification protocol: the bank requires the board resolution authorizing the account and the subscription/escrow agreement, plus the foreign investor's source-of-funds confirmation. Statistics Canada cross-border transaction reporting triggers monthly reporting obligations; the corporation must maintain the underlying legal records, T2/T106 corporate tax filings, T1134 foreign-affiliate information returns where applicable, and must update the Alberta Register of Beneficial Ownership within the statutory 15-day window. Caution: if the inbound financing is structured as shareholder-indebtedness, Canada's thin-capitalization rules under subsection 18(4)-(6) apply at a 1.5:1 debt-to-equity ratio relative to specified non-resident shareholder debt; must keep the equity escrow ledger and intercompany loan ledger fully segregated to preserve evidence of legal characterization, and the borrower must file Form T106 for intercompany interest reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use tiered clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 (single corporate payment) for all vendor, contractor, data-center and distribution settlements; include the beneficiary bank SWIFT/BIC and local settlement system (Fedwire/CHIPS for USD); (ii) SWIFT MT202 (bank-to-bank cover) where an intermediate correspondent is required for non-CAD cross-border jurisdictions; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary credit) under UCP600 / eUCP for procurement of hardware, real-property data infrastructure, or tenant-screening data from foreign suppliers requiring bank undertakings; (iv) Canadian domestic CAD disbursements via Lynx (Payments Canada large-value settlement system) for high-value treasury transfers and via ACSS/EFT (Automated Clearing Settlement System) with Pre-authorized Debit (PAD) agreements for recurring payroll and vendor payments; (v) USD operating sweeps through the bank's internal notional pooling between the USD and CAD operating accounts at daily cut-off; (vi) Stripe Billing settlements: card-network payments (Visa/Mastercard/AMEX) settle through Stripe Payments Canada to the CA_CORP operating account as T+2 CAD institutional ACSS settlements; (vii) ACH Direct collections from US-domiciled tenants/subscribers: route via the Canadian bank's cross-border ACH/NACHA service (generic SEC codes CCD for business and WEB for consumer internet-initiated debits) or via the fintech partner's US clearing account; ensure all outgoing MT103 messages include ISO 20022 purpose codes and reference the underlying commercial invoice, the CRA Business Number (BN), and the customer contract ID for automatic reconciliation in the treasury management system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright CAD/USD deliverable forward contracts (plain vanilla, tenors up to 24 months) executed under an ISDA 1998 FX Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex (CSA) with the Schedule I counterparty bank.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible emerging-market exposure legs (e.g., CNY, NGN, ARS, EGP) where the PropTech SaaS platform invoices local tenants, vendors, or data providers and Canadian banks are permitted to book NDFs referencing fully non-deliverable currencies.

Cross-Currency Swaps (XCCY) for long-dated hedging of foreign-investor capital, intercompany loans, and acquisition-currency liabilities (CAD/USD and CAD/EUR) with mark-to-market CSA collateral posting and regulatory margin compliance under OSFI non-centrally-cleared derivatives margin rules (Guideline B-7).

European-style FX options and zero-cost collars purchased from the bank's dealing desk for translation hedging of USD-denominated subscription revenue into CAD, subject to the entity's internal treasury policy requiring board-approved option-notional limits.

FX swaps (rollovers) for intra-month treasury cash-flow bridging between the CAD Operating Account and foreign-currency disbursement accounts, allowing conversion at a near leg with a pre-agreed far leg and no open-market FX risk at maturity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta or authorized registry agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each incorporation anniversary; confirm registered office, directors and corporate status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No monetary late fee; Registrar issues Notice of Intent to Dissolve; continued default triggers administrative strike-off; revival requires outstanding annual returns, CAD 300 revival fee and Registrar consent

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return with Alberta corporate tax (AT1) schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (December 31 year-end: due June 30 next year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12%; 10% plus 2% per month on repeat failure; daily compound interest at prescribed rate; director liability for unremitted withholdings (ITA s. 227.1)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Return (Excise Tax Act) - annual, quarterly, or monthly by registrant status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers: within 3 months after fiscal year-end; quarterly and monthly filers: within 1 month after reporting period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 5% late-filing penalty plus 1% per full month up to 12%; prescribed-rate daily interest; penalties for false statements or omissions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T4 Statement of Remuneration Paid and T4 Summary (payroll informational returns)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of February following the calendar year in which remuneration was paid
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 25 per day per slip, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500 (CAD 25,000 for corporations); additional penalties for deliberate omissions

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to offering/reporting issuers and entities listed on TSX/TSXV; private non-offering PropTech corporations may waive auditor appointment by unanimous shareholder consent, renewable for up to 5 years (ABCA s. 159); when appointed, the auditor is elected at the annual general meeting, which must be held within 6 months after fiscal year-end and within 15 months of the preceding meeting
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) for public/reporting issuers; ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) available to private enterprises; SaaS revenue recognized under IFRS 15; real-estate platform fees and provincial tax components integrated with the federal corporate return

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: ABCA requires non-public corporations to keep an internal Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC); record individuals holding 25% or more of voting shares or with de facto control; update the register within 15 days of any share transfer or control change and re-confirm annually at fiscal year-end; the register is not publicly filed in Alberta but must be produced on demand to the Registrar, CRA, and law-enforcement; the Alberta annual return confirms directors and registered office only, not UBO names
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (share register and transfer ledger)
Register of Directors (names, addresses, and notice dates)
Minute Book (AGM and board minutes, by-laws, unanimous shareholder resolutions)
Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 75-450 (CAD 100-600) per year for Alberta registered office / registered agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,500-26,000 (CAD 10,000-35,000) for a first-year full audit of a private PropTech SaaS corporation at a mid-tier Canadian accounting firm

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% composed of 15% federal Part I rate and 8% Alberta general corporate rate; reduced to 11% (9% federal + 2% Alberta) for a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) eligible for the small business deduction on active business income up to CAD 500,000 (federal allocation) and Alberta's CAD 500,000 threshold
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED investment tax credit: refundable 35% of qualifying R&D expenditures up to CAD 3 million for CCPCs, plus non-refundable 15% on excess; Alberta Innovation Employment Grant provides 20% cash rebate on eligible R&D and commercialization expenditures up to CAD 1 million annually; accelerated capital cost allowance for qualifying clean-energy and zero-emission technology assets

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; mandatory electronic filing via CRA E-file using certified tax preparation software (e.g., Intuit Profile, Taxprep, UFile) or through a jurisdiction-approved service provider
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; instalment payments are required quarterly when net tax payable exceeds CAD 3,000
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return must be filed within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; final tax balance due within 2 months (or 3 months for a CCPC claiming the small business deduction on active business income) after the fiscal year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computed in accordance with Parts I and IV, including business income, property income, and capital gains; for interprovincial allocation the Alberta allocation factor is reported on Schedule 5
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income from carrying on a business in Canada through a permanent establishment (PE); if no PE in Canada, line 101 is nil unless Part XIV branch tax applies; allocate income to Alberta based on Schedule 5 if a PE exists in Alberta

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal basic tax computed by applying the Part I rates; indicates head-office or provincial factors for the Alberta jurisdiction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations compute Part I tax on Canadian-source business income only; federal Part I tax is reduced by the treaty-allocation factor and then Part XIV branch tax (25%) applies on net Canadian income after adjustment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total federal tax payable, provincial tax payable to Alberta (including Alberta corporate income tax at 8%), investment tax credits, and refundable credits (e.g., SR&ED ITC)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents compute provincial tax only if an Alberta PE exists; otherwise the amount is nil. Provide T2 Schedule 5 to confirm allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Canadian dividends received deduction, intra-group financing adjustment, and other taxable reductions to income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Typically inapplicable to non-resident filers unless receiving Canadian-source dividends from a Canadian corporation; Part XIII withholding tax is separately reported on NR4 or T2 Schedule ?

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed statement of contributed surplus, retained earnings, and capital stock necessary to substantiate tax balances on liquidation or dividend declarations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete Schedule 10 fully for all shareholders resident outside Canada to support Part XIII withholding tax filings and to document the eligible capital dividend account for non-taxable dividend distributions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty is 5% of the unpaid tax balance plus 1% per full month up to 12% for returns filed more than 3 months late; repeated omission penalty increases to 10% and 2% per month up to 20%; gross negligence penalty under s.163(2) is 50% of the understated tax, plus interest compounded daily on all unpaid balances; willful evasion under s.238 and Criminal Code s.239 may result in fines up to CAD 1,000,000 and imprisonment of up to 8 years

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid or credited to a non-resident of Canada, unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty (e.g., Canada-US Convention: 15% general, 5% if the shareholder is a corporation that owns at least 10% of the voting stock directly and is the beneficial owner)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must provide the Canadian withholding agent (payer or custodian) with a completed Form NR301 (Certificate of Residency) or, where applicable, Form NR302 (for reduced withholding under a treaty), containing a certification of residency issued by the competent authority of the residence state; the payer must retain the form and cannot apply the reduced rate unless the form has been received prior to or within a reasonable time after the payment. The foreign tax authority's residency certificate (e.g., US IRS Form 6166, UK Form CRS-1) is sufficient if it is accepted by the CRA; failing to hold the certificate on file exposes the payer to liability for the difference at the statutory 25% rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate is 25% on royalties and 25% on interest; under Canada-US DTA, arm's-length interest is generally exempt (0%) while non-arm's-length interest is 15%; royalty withholding is 10% (or 0% for certain industrial, computer software, and cultural property under limited circumstances); with other major treaty partners, typical rates range 5%–15% on interest and 10%–15% on royalties

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory contemporaneous documentation thresholds under Canadian Income Tax Act s.247(4): the taxpayer's gross revenue for the taxation year exceeds CAD 5 million, and the aggregate fair market value of all hard-to-value intangibles, interest, royalties, management fees, and purchase/sale transactions with each non-arm's length non-resident exceeds CAD 1 million in the year; penalties for failure to prepare adequate documentation are waived only if complete and contemporaneous records exist and are provided to the CRA within 30 days of a written request
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not impose a separate Economic Substance Regulations regime, but the CRA applies a robust 'economic reality' assessment via the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s.245) and the statutory transfer-pricing rule (s.247). A transaction without commercial economic substance and lacking business purpose will be disregarded; intercompany fees, management charges, or royalty streams that do not align with actual services rendered, personnel, and assets are vulnerable to reallocation as amounts that would have been agreed upon at arm's length; for a PropTech SaaS, the relevant economic activities (software development, data hosting, customer contract management, and risk control) must be conducted by Canadian employees and supported by payroll, technical infrastructure, and management records to avoid substance-based reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (Willful Understatement of Digital Commerce Revenue)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to report or suppressing subscription revenues from SaaS users, rental screening or payment-processing fees paid by ACH/Direct or Stripe, or diverting revenue to an undisclosed offshore shell account; creating fictitious invoices to conceal revenue; making misleading statements to the CRA during an audit of the T2 return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary penalty of 50% of the amount of tax understated under s.163(2), plus daily compound interest; summary conviction under s.238 of the Income Tax Act carries a fine not exceeding CAD 10,000 and/or six months imprisonment; indictment under Criminal Code s.380 (fraud) may expose the corporation to fines of up to CAD 100,000, and responsible individuals to imprisonment up to 14 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate directors who knowingly participate in or direct evasion are jointly and severally liable under s.160(5) for amounts that the CRA cannot otherwise collect; civil restitution orders may attach personal assets, travel bans are imposed under the Criminal Code, and imprisonment up to 14 years may be ordered; for repeated evader directors, the CRA may request director residency restrictions and overseas pass revocation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Economic Substance Abuse / GAAR
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing a tax-haven corporation (e.g., in the Cayman Islands or Bermuda) with no physical office, employees, or substantial business activities solely to invoice Canadian SaaS revenue and avoid Canadian corporate tax; artificially rotating intellectual property to a foreign affiliate and paying excessive deductible royalties/charges to strip profits from Alberta; entering into circular financing with a related foreign entity to manufacture artificial tax deductions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA will recompute income under s.247 and s.245 denying the deduction or benefit; a penalty equal to 50% of the tax benefit from GAAR avoidance transaction (s.245(4)) plus interest; gross negligence penalties of 50% under s.163(2) may also apply; the classification as a 'foreign-controlled private corporation' or 'non-resident-owned corporation' may trigger additional reporting requirements such as T1146, T1134, and Form T106 penalties of CAD 2,500 per form
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorized the sham transactions can be held personally liable for corporate tax under s.227.1 (Part XIII withholding) if the shell entity becomes insolvent; for participation in fraudulent transactions, civil liability for the tax shortfall plus punitive damages; the CRA may seek regional court injunctions preventing the sale of personal assets and, in egregious cases, a director may be subject to a travel restriction while the tax investigation is pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PropTech platform to accept proceeds of fraud while failing to register under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) after exceeding CAD 10,000 in cash or equivalent transactions in a 24-hour period; ignoring prescribed record-keeping, client identification, and reporting obligations under the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) regime
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties under PCMLTFA up to CAD 2 million for corporations (and CAD 1 million for individuals) for each violation; criminal penalties for laundering proceeds under Criminal Code s.462.31 include imprisonment for up to 10 years; seizure, restraint, and forfeiture of the SaaS accounts, bank balances, and connected real-estate holdings; the stock exchange or payment services (Stripe, ACH network) may suspend or terminate services, causing contractual liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and compliance officers may be exposed to police prosecution if they knowingly or negligently conduct a prohibited financial transaction; criminal sanctions include imprisonment up to 5 years for failing to report a suspicious transaction, loss of professional credentialing, personal fines up to CAD 500,000, and lifetime disqualification from serving as a director of any Canadian corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act if convicted of an indictable offence.
